findings.title: Spawned flusher processes fail the process type check
findings.body: The spawn context creates multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess instances, which inherit BaseProcess rather than multiprocessing.Process. This isinstance check is therefore false for production flushers, so a hung worker is never killed before its handle is overwritten by the replacement. If the old worker recovers, both workers operate on the same shards and share heartbeat/backpressure state, undermining hang detection and leaving an untracked worker. Check against BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threading.Thread instead. The termination check in join has the same type mismatch.

findings.title: Terminate remaining workers after the join deadline expires
findings.body: When the deadline is consumed by next_step.join or by waiting for an earlier worker, this break skips shutdown handling for every remaining worker. Setting stopped is cooperative: a worker blocked in Redis or Kafka future.result() cannot observe it and can survive join and the subsequent partition rebalance. Exhausting the timeout should stop waiting, but all remaining processes still need to be terminated and reaped rather than skipped.
